# Supplementary experiments (E01-E09)

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_supplementary.py from results/supplementary/.
     Edit the CSV files or index.yaml there, not this file. -->

These tables are supplementary results reported by the authors of the paper. They
extend the paper's tables with broader guidance edits, deeper compositions, cost and
annotation accounting, a label sweep for the factorised variant and related-method
controls. The numbers are stored as CSV files in
[`results/supplementary/`](../results/supplementary/) and loaded with
`sigma.supplementary`; the figures are in
[`assets/results/`](../assets/results/README.md) and the commands and
configurations for each experiment are listed in the
[README](../README.md#supplementary-experiments).

Unless stated otherwise: backbone Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with LoRA (rank 16), 10 labeled examples per intent, five seeds (13, 21, 42, 87, 100), frozen parameters at test time. Accuracy is in percent and differences are in percentage points (pp). Comp. is the mean accuracy over the held-out guidance-composition conditions (composition depths 2/4/8, with and without the reversal). Changed is the accuracy on test instances whose required output changes under the edited guidance. GPU-hours cover training only.

## Transfer to broader guidance edits and deeper compositions

Paraphrased descriptions, random serialisation, cross-group binding swaps, and binding paths of depth 8 and 16.

<a id="e01"></a>

### E01. Frozen transfer to paraphrased descriptions, random serialisation and cross-group binding swaps

*Extends Tables 1 and 12 of the paper.*

**Question.** Do models trained on sibling swaps and one reversal transfer to broader edits of the guidance?

**Setup.**

- Frozen 10-shot models; no further training on the new conditions.
- Paraphrased descriptions: equivalent paraphrases of the class descriptions, verified independently of test outcomes, combined with held-out compositions.
- Random serialisation: randomised child orders (beyond the single reversal used in training), combined with compositions.
- Cross-group binding: binding swaps across sibling groups, beyond the sibling swaps used in training, combined with compositions.
- SIGMA-F receives the same updated descriptions and binding map.
- Scope: transfer within a fixed semantic task and candidate inventory.
- Each cell: Comp. / changed-target accuracy (%).

| Dataset | Frozen test condition | Paired SFT | Transported KL | SIGMA | SIGMA-F |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | Paraphrased descriptions + compositions | 83.90 / 67.00 | 85.45 / 72.20 | 87.20 / 80.80 | 89.20 / 88.90 |
| BANKING77 | Random serialization + compositions | 84.60 / 68.30 | 85.95 / 73.20 | 87.85 / 82.00 | 89.91 / 89.54 |
| BANKING77 | Cross-group binding compositions | 77.80 / 43.50 | 79.50 / 48.00 | 82.60 / 58.50 | 89.91 / 89.30 |
| CLINC150 | Paraphrased descriptions + compositions | 91.85 / 78.40 | 92.75 / 82.00 | 94.65 / 88.80 | 95.65 / 95.40 |
| CLINC150 | Random serialization + compositions | 92.40 / 79.80 | 93.20 / 83.50 | 94.90 / 89.50 | 96.25 / 96.13 |
| CLINC150 | Cross-group binding compositions | 88.50 / 55.00 | 89.50 / 60.00 | 91.50 / 70.00 | 96.25 / 95.80 |
| HWU64 | Paraphrased descriptions + compositions | 84.55 / 66.80 | 85.45 / 71.50 | 87.65 / 80.50 | 89.80 / 89.50 |
| HWU64 | Random serialization + compositions | 84.80 / 67.80 | 86.10 / 72.90 | 88.15 / 81.80 | 90.49 / 90.60 |
| HWU64 | Cross-group binding compositions | 76.80 / 42.00 | 78.60 / 47.50 | 81.90 / 57.00 | 90.49 / 90.40 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA exceeds both direct-scoring controls (paired SFT, transported KL) in every condition.
- On cross-group swaps SIGMA reaches 58.50 / 70.00 / 57.00% changed-target accuracy, +10.5 / +10.0 / +9.5 pp over transported KL.
- SIGMA-F (exact lookup) is highest in every condition.

Data: [`01_transfer_and_composition/E01_broader_guidance_edits.csv`](../results/supplementary/01_transfer_and_composition/E01_broader_guidance_edits.csv)
<a id="e02"></a>

### E02. Local residuals and accuracy along unseen binding paths of depth 8 and 16

*Extends Figure 6, Eq. (7) of the paper.*

**Question.** How large are the local residuals of the composition bound on entirely unseen, longer binding paths?

**Setup.**

- Frozen models evaluated on held-out binding paths using all 77 / 150 / 64 candidates.
- The bound of Eq. (7) and the certificate of Corollary B.4 are stated for any valid path; the residuals eps_j = ||u_j - P_j u_{j-1}||_2 are measured on the unseen paths themselves.
- Reported at the two largest depths; depth 16 is the final stress test.
- Each cell: median path-average local residual / all-path Comp. accuracy (%). Accuracy covers all sampled paths, including initially incorrect predictions.

| Dataset | Depth | Paired SFT | Transported KL | SIGMA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | 8 | 0.44 / 84.67 | 0.35 / 86.23 | 0.25 / 88.09 |
| BANKING77 | 16 | 0.49 / 82.40 | 0.39 / 84.00 | 0.29 / 85.70 |
| CLINC150 | 8 | 0.38 / 92.85 | 0.30 / 93.67 | 0.21 / 95.00 |
| CLINC150 | 16 | 0.42 / 90.50 | 0.34 / 91.70 | 0.24 / 93.50 |
| HWU64 | 8 | 0.50 / 85.55 | 0.41 / 86.44 | 0.30 / 88.68 |
| HWU64 | 16 | 0.55 / 82.50 | 0.46 / 84.00 | 0.34 / 86.00 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA has the lowest residuals and the highest accuracy at both depths on every dataset.
- The certificate stays conditional on each path's residuals and initial margin.

Data: [`01_transfer_and_composition/E02_composition_depth_residuals.csv`](../results/supplementary/01_transfer_and_composition/E02_composition_depth_residuals.csv)

## Annotation efficiency and training cost

SIGMA with 4 shots against LoRA-SFT with 16 shots, and equal training-time caps.

<a id="e03"></a>

### E03. SIGMA-4 vs. SFT-16: training labels, development labels and training GPU-hours

*Extends Tables 5 and 8 of the paper.*

**Question.** Does the annotation saving survive when development labels and training time are counted?

**Setup.**

- Combines the Table 5 accuracies with measured training time under the same hardware and accounting settings.
- At 10 shots, SIGMA costs 75.1% more than single-view SFT and 4.2% more than paired SFT using the same views (Table 8).
- GPU-hours are approximate and cover training only.

| Dataset | Training labels: 4 / 16 shots | Train + dev labels: 4 / 16 shots | SIGMA-4: Comp. (%) / GPU-h | SFT-16: Comp. (%) / GPU-h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | 308 / 1232 | 1848 / 2772 | 85.72 / ≈5.49 | 82.61 / ≈12.54 |
| CLINC150 | 600 / 2400 | 3600 / 5400 | 93.42 / ≈20.84 | 91.54 / ≈47.60 |
| HWU64 | 256 / 1024 | 1332 / 2100 | 85.28 / ≈3.79 | 83.14 / ≈8.67 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA-4 beats SFT-16 on Comp. with 75% fewer training labels and about 56% less training time.
- Counting development labels too, the savings are 33.3% / 33.3% / 36.6%.

Data: [`02_annotation_efficiency_and_cost/E03_sigma4_vs_sft16_labels_and_gpu.csv`](../results/supplementary/02_annotation_efficiency_and_cost/E03_sigma4_vs_sft16_labels_and_gpu.csv)
<a id="e04"></a>

### E04. Equal training-time caps on BANKING77 (10 shots)

*Extends Tables 8 and 11 of the paper.*

**Question.** Does SIGMA keep its advantage when every method gets the same training-time budget?

**Setup.**

- BANKING77, 10 shots, five seeds; each run stops when training finishes or the cap is reached.
- Two caps: 7.84 GPU-h and 13.73 GPU-h.
- The LoRA-SFT row at the 13.73 GPU-h cap is the token-matched control of Table 11.

| Method | 7.84 GPU-h cap: Comp. (%) | 13.73 GPU-h cap: actual GPU-h / Comp. (%) |
|---|---:|---:|
| LoRA-SFT | 80.96 | 13.51 / 80.43 |
| Paired SFT | 82.10 | 13.18 / 85.37 |
| Transported KL | 83.45 | 13.46 / 86.83 |
| SIGMA | 85.90 | 13.73 / 88.56 |
| SIGMA-F | 89.50 | 8.11 / 89.91 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA retains its advantage over the direct-scoring baselines under the lower cap.
- SIGMA-F finishes in 8.11 GPU-h and is the most accurate at both caps.

Data: [`02_annotation_efficiency_and_cost/E04_equal_training_time_caps.csv`](../results/supplementary/02_annotation_efficiency_and_cost/E04_equal_training_time_caps.csv)

## SIGMA and the factorised variant SIGMA-F

Label sweep over 1/2/4/8/16 shots and the 4-shot training cost.

<a id="e05"></a>

### E05. SIGMA vs. SIGMA-F over the 1/2/4/8/16-shot label budgets

*Extends Table 5 of the paper.*

**Question.** How does the factorised alternative SIGMA-F compare across label budgets?

**Setup.**

- SIGMA-F predicts the semantic class, then applies an exact binding lookup (Appendix A.3); both methods receive the same descriptions and map.
- Matched LoRA capacity, five seeds; nested training subsets, shared development sets, evaluation samples and weights.
- SIGMA values are those of Table 5. Entries: Comp. accuracy, mean ± SD (%).
- Because of exact lookup, SIGMA-F's Base and Comp. accuracies are identical on matched samples and weights.

| Dataset | Method | 1 shot | 2 shots | 4 shots | 8 shots | 16 shots |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | SIGMA | 73.81 ± 2.13 | 81.26 ± 1.75 | 85.72 ± 1.13 | 88.01 ± 0.96 | 89.47 ± 0.76 |
| BANKING77 | SIGMA-F | 75.80 ± 2.00 | 82.10 ± 1.55 | 86.30 ± 1.18 | 89.10 ± 0.86 | 91.10 ± 0.62 |
| CLINC150 | SIGMA | 85.47 ± 1.96 | 90.31 ± 1.75 | 93.42 ± 1.12 | 95.01 ± 0.98 | 95.81 ± 0.74 |
| CLINC150 | SIGMA-F | 86.90 ± 1.75 | 90.90 ± 1.30 | 93.80 ± 1.00 | 95.85 ± 0.70 | 96.70 ± 0.48 |
| HWU64 | SIGMA | 72.65 ± 1.97 | 80.41 ± 1.60 | 85.28 ± 1.30 | 88.37 ± 1.03 | 89.91 ± 0.79 |
| HWU64 | SIGMA-F | 75.10 ± 2.10 | 82.00 ± 1.65 | 86.10 ± 1.28 | 90.05 ± 0.92 | 91.35 ± 0.62 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA-F has the higher Comp. mean at every budget on all three datasets.
- When the semantic-class interface and the binding map are available at inference, exact lookup is the stronger choice; SIGMA improves the model's own use of the guidance text (+3.19 / +1.95 / +2.97 pp Comp. over paired SFT, Table 13).
- The 75% training-label saving refers to SIGMA-4 vs. SFT-16 (E03).

Data: [`03_sigma_vs_sigma_f/E05_sigma_vs_sigma_f_label_sweep.csv`](../results/supplementary/03_sigma_vs_sigma_f/E05_sigma_vs_sigma_f_label_sweep.csv)

## Related-method controls

A PBM-LoRA-style control, Symbol-Tuning-style binding augmentation, and paired gains with 95% intervals.

<a id="e07"></a>

### E07. PBM-LoRA adapted to paired supervision vs. transported KL and SIGMA

*Extends Tables 1 and 12 of the paper.*

**Question.** How does SIGMA compare with permutation-consistency training in the style of PBM-LoRA?

**Setup.**

- PBM-adapted + paired CE keeps PBM-LoRA's log-probability dispersion and entropy terms.
- Its multi-permutation protocol is adapted to two guidance views, full-sequence (aligned) candidate probabilities and matched LoRA capacity, with at most 15 search trials.
- SIGMA's centred loss removes the common score offset and penalises discrepancies in all transported pairwise log-odds exactly (Appendix B.1).
- 10-shot accuracies (%). Changed = changed targets.

| Dataset | KL Comp. | PBM-adapted Comp. | SIGMA Comp. | PBM-adapted Changed | SIGMA Changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | 86.83 | 87.55 | 88.56 | 77.00 | 83.18 |
| CLINC150 | 94.17 | 94.70 | **95.37** | 86.00 | 90.42 |
| HWU64 | 86.94 | 87.55 | 89.08 | 76.00 | 83.23 |

**Key findings.**

- SIGMA exceeds the PBM-adapted control on Comp. (+1.01 / +0.67 / +1.53 pp) and on changed targets (+6.18 / +4.42 / +7.23 pp).

Data: [`04_related_method_baselines/E07_pbm_lora_adapted.csv`](../results/supplementary/04_related_method_baselines/E07_pbm_lora_adapted.csv)
<a id="e08"></a>

### E08. Symbol-Tuning-style global binding augmentation, with and without SIGMA alignment

*Extends Table 10 of the paper.*

**Question.** Does alignment still help on top of Symbol-Tuning-style mapping augmentation?

**Setup.**

- Opaque output IDs and global random bindings sampled independently of the gold label; the schema supplies the mapping that in-context examples supply in Symbol Tuning.
- Both variants use the same augmentation and paired supervision, so the difference isolates the alignment term.
- Entries: Comp. accuracy (%).

| Dataset | Global binding augmentation + paired CE | Same augmentation + SIGMA alignment | Gain (pp) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | 86.85 | 88.10 | +1.25 |
| CLINC150 | 93.95 | 94.95 | +1.00 |
| HWU64 | 86.50 | 88.20 | +1.70 |

**Key findings.**

- Alignment adds 1.00-1.70 pp on top of global binding augmentation.

Data: [`04_related_method_baselines/E08_symbol_tuning_style_augmentation.csv`](../results/supplementary/04_related_method_baselines/E08_symbol_tuning_style_augmentation.csv)
<a id="e09"></a>

### E09. SIGMA's composition gains over paired SFT and transported KL with 95% intervals

*Extends Tables 12 and 13 of the paper.*

**Question.** Are the gains over paired SFT and transported KL distinguishable from zero?

**Setup.**

- Table 13: Comp. gains with paired pointwise 95% intervals.
- Table 12: gains on test examples whose required answer changes.

| Dataset | SIGMA − paired SFT, Comp. (pp) [95% CI] | SIGMA − transported KL, Comp. (pp) [95% CI] | SIGMA − transported KL, changed targets (pp) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BANKING77 | +3.19 [2.63, 3.76] | +1.73 [1.19, 2.25] | 8.80 |
| CLINC150 | +1.95 [1.48, 2.43] | +1.20 [0.79, 1.64] | 6.15 |
| HWU64 | +2.97 [2.38, 3.59] | +2.14 [1.57, 2.72] | 9.65 |

**Key findings.**

- All six Comp. gains have 95% intervals above zero.
- Gains are much larger on examples that require a different answer (8.80 / 6.15 / 9.65 pp over transported KL).

Data: [`04_related_method_baselines/E09_paired_gains_with_ci.csv`](../results/supplementary/04_related_method_baselines/E09_paired_gains_with_ci.csv)
